8.6K views · 56 reactions | NASA'S SPHEREX MISSION LAUNCHES FROM VANDENBURG TUESDAY NIGHT:

At 8:10pm on Tuesday night, March 11 of 2025, NASA's SPHEREx mission was launched by SpaceX at Vandenburg Space Forse Base. The mission was responsible for launching the Observatory and PUNCH satellites.

The mission had been previously delayed, however all was a go Tuesday night for the successful launch. For more information about the launch, please visit the following link from the SpaceX website:

https://www.spacex.com/launches/mission/?missionId=spherex | Safety for Citizens

excerpts.text: SPHEREx was successfully launched on March 11, 2025.

## Launch

SPHEREx was launched aboard a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket from Space Launch Complex 4 East (SLC-4E) at the Vandenberg Space Force Base, California on March 11, 2025. The launch was procured by NASA's Launch Services Program and was conducted as a shared mission with the Polarimeter to UNify the Corona and Heliosphere (PUNCH) spacecraft.

* August 03, 2022: NASA confirmed that SPHEREx will launch alongside the PUNCH (Polarimeter to Unify the Corona and Heliosphere) mission as a secondary rideshare payload. This decision optimizes launch costs and aligns with mission requirements. 13)

excerpts.text: NASA’s SPHEREx (Spectro-Photometer for the History of the Universe, Epoch of Reionization and Ices Explorer) observatory and PUNCH (Polarimeter to Unify the Corona and Heliosphere) satellites lift off on a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket from Vandenberg Space Force Base in California on March 11, 2025.

PDT on March 11 aboard a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket from Space Launch Complex 4 East at Vandenberg Space Force Base in California.

Launching together into low Earth orbit, NASA’s SPHEREx and PUNCH missions will study a range of topics from the early universe to our nearest star.

Riding with [SPHEREx](https://www.jpl.nasa.gov/missions/spherex/) aboard the Falcon 9 were four small satellites that make up the agency’s [PUNCH](https://science.nasa.gov/mission/punch/) (Polarimeter to Unify the Corona and Heliosphere) mission, which will study how the Sun’s outer atmosphere becomes the solar wind.
